run.title: The Road to Candlekeep Is Paved with Bad Decisions
run.overview:
PREMISE
Vhalrix the Recall-Eater stole the Shield of the Hidden Lord to consume the infernal power imprisoned within it. The shield defended itself by forming a contained Hell from the memories it absorbed while traveling with the party. Vhalrix pulled the characters inside because their memories are the keys to opening the prison. They must reclaim three Truths, defeat Vhalrix, recover the shield, and decide which of two possible heroes returns.

CURRENT MISSION
The party was traveling to Candlekeep with a shield they do not understand. A demon ambushed them and escaped with it. If they survive this realm, Candlekeep remains their destination.

PARTY NOTES
• Dax Darkmoon — level 5 Shadar-kai Soulknife rogue. Secretly hates the Flaming Fist after watching its soldiers abuse civilians during a night of reconnaissance. Do not force him to disclose it.
• Eldara — level 5 elf Battle Master. Give her direct physical objectives and a clear enemy rather than demanding introspection.
• Jon Meatshield — level 4 Kalashtar barbarian, likely absent. If present, give him the real DC 20 gate in The Warning They Ignored. Run one fewer minion if absent.
• Korrath Drakenscale — level 5 dragonborn Conquest paladin. Replaced Brody and shares Brody's player. The final choice belongs entirely to this player.
• Morn — level 4 half-orc Life cleric. Former soldier carrying the weight of a failure; functionally the party healer. His remedy shield contains a vial he did not place there.
• Ori Maru — level 5 Githyanki Psi Warrior. Keep dialogue optional and let observation or decisive action communicate for him.
• New character — the Unwritten. The realm has no memories of this character and cannot rewrite them. Once per scene, the player may ask what detail does not belong; answer with a useful seam, false memory, exit, or vulnerability.

RUNNING PRINCIPLES
Keep the recap darkly funny but factual, not punitive. Let players correct false memories aloud. Never make roleplay confession the only solution. The surprise is Brody's opportunity to return; the cost of that choice must be explained clearly and privately. Bring everyone to level 5 if practical, and rebuild Brody at level 5 if he returns.

THE THREE TRUTHS
Truth of the Song cancels one group fear, illusion, or psychic effect in the finale. Truth of the Dead leaves one falling character at 1 HP instead. Truth of the Warning turns one successful attack against a party member into a complete miss. Use physical tokens if possible.

scenes.title: Table Briefing — Is That Your Answer?
scenes.purpose: Set the table contract for a character-focused one-shot before the recap, jokes, dice, or in-fiction manipulation begin.
scenes.readAloud: Tonight is more character-focused than our usual game. Humor is welcome, but when a scene puts a serious choice in front of your character, I’m going to ask, ‘Is that your answer?’ Before you answer, you can ask me what your character understands or what the immediate stakes appear to be. Whatever you confirm becomes true in the adventure and will affect the finale. You can answer through words or actions—you do not need to perform a monologue.
scenes.secrets: This is an out-of-character table agreement, not Vhalrix speaking and not an in-world threat. The players should understand the rule before their characters enter the contained Hell.
scenes.notes:
AT A GLANCE
Goal: establish the table rule for serious character choices before any fiction begins.
Timebox: 5 minutes.
End condition: every player understands what confirmation means; then immediately start Scene 2 — The Road Folds.

BEFORE YOU START
• Keep this scene out of character. Vhalrix is not speaking.
• Have Quick capture ready with the type set to Decision.
• Do not begin the recap or ask for a roll yet.

RUN IT STEP BY STEP
1. Tell the table this one-shot will be more character-focused than the usual game.
2. Read the Read aloud text exactly or in your own words.
3. Emphasize that humor remains welcome and roleplay may be expressed through actions.
4. Tell them they may ask what their character understands and what the immediate stakes appear to be before answering.
5. Explain the confirmation sequence: you describe the choice and stakes; the player responds; you ask, ‘Is that your answer?’; only their confirmation locks it in.
6. Ask, ‘Does anyone have a question about how that will work?’ Answer procedural questions now.
7. Once everyone understands, say, ‘Good. Last time, a demon escaped with your shield.’ Move directly into Scene 2.

WHEN TO ASK ‘IS THAT YOUR ANSWER?’
Use it only for a deliberate character choice with meaningful consequences. State or clarify the immediate stakes first. Never use it to trap a player who misunderstood the fiction.

WHAT COUNTS AS AN ANSWER
Dialogue, a declared action, an explicit refusal, or silence paired with an unmistakable action can be confirmed. A speech, accent, confession, or theatrical performance is never required.

WHAT DOES NOT COUNT
Jokes, cross-talk, rules discussion, tentative brainstorming, questions, or out-of-character frustration are not answers. If the player has not confirmed, the choice is not final.

AFTER A CONFIRMATION
Repeat the decision in one plain sentence: ‘Your answer is that Dax keeps this private.’ Record it in Quick capture as a Decision. Let it alter later fiction or the finale; do not immediately punish it merely to prove the rule matters.

TABLE SAFETY
Confirmation locks a fictional decision. It is not consent to uncomfortable content. If a player seems genuinely distressed, stop the fiction and check in out of character.

CUT FOR TIME
Do not cut the spoken contract. If everyone understands immediately, skip examples and begin Scene 2.

scenes.title: The Road Folds
scenes.purpose: Bring the wife-seeking stranger into the party at the moment of the theft, pull everyone into the contained Hell, and establish why the realm cannot rewrite him.
scenes.readAloud:
Candlekeep remains a dark tooth against the horizon, never drawing closer. Behind you, the road repeats: the same dead tree, the same overturned milestone, the same smear of black blood.

Then the stolen shield screams.

The sound comes from beneath your feet. The road splits like wet paper, revealing fire below—and something in that fire is singing the Elfsong backward.
scenes.secrets:
Vhalrix did not escape cleanly. The shield trapped the demon inside its emergency prison, caught every nearby witness in the infernal wake, and pulled in anything metaphysically tethered to Vhalrix. The imprisoned intelligence within the shield is helping the party only because Vhalrix threatens it; it remains an unreliable ally.

The stranger has never encountered the shield, so the realm possesses no stored memories of him. Vhalrix should know him through the memories stolen from his wife, but she protected him by feeding the demon contradictory names, faces, voices, and histories. The realm can perceive him but cannot write a coherent version of him. Do not reveal her resistance until The Fifth Portrait.
scenes.notes:
AT A GLANCE
Goal: introduce the Unwritten without having him appear from nowhere, trap everyone inside the shield's memory-Hell, and land the party in the Elfsong.
Timebox: 10 minutes.
End condition: everyone lands in the empty Elfsong; the party knows the thief and shield are trapped here; the Unwritten knows his special question.
Do not ask for initiative or a saving throw. The fall must happen.

BEFORE YOU START
• Ask the Unwritten's player for his wife's name if you do not have it. Write it down.
• Ask what small personal object of hers he would recognize instantly. This object hangs among Vhalrix's trophies and returns after the final battle. Write it down.
• Remind yourself: her disappearance led him toward Candlekeep. He reaches the road seconds after the theft.

RUN IT STEP BY STEP
1. Address the Unwritten first: ‘Your wife disappeared from your home in the middle of the night. Every trail eventually narrowed to Candlekeep and this road. As you crest the rise, you see a battered group watching a demon vanish into flame with a blackened shield. Hanging among its trophies is [HER OBJECT].’
2. Tell the party: ‘A lone stranger reaches the ruined road just as the demon disappears.’ Give them only a heartbeat to register one another.
3. Describe Vhalrix looking directly at the stranger with confusion. Say: ‘It knows it should remember you. It cannot.’ Do not explain why yet.
4. Read the group Read aloud text. Candlekeep recedes, the road repeats, the stolen shield screams, and the ground tears open.
5. If a character tries to fly, teleport, grab someone, or resist, let the action change how they land or whom they protect. It cannot prevent entry into the realm. Do not call the attempt useless.
6. Ask each returning player: ‘As you fall, one image from your journey appears around you. What does your character see?’ One sentence each is enough.
7. If someone cannot remember, offer: the Elfsong, the bathhouse door, Amrik's table, Brody's empty place, or the shield vanishing. This is not a memory test.
8. Address the Unwritten: ‘Everyone else falls through places they recognize. The fire reaches for your history and finds incompatible faces, wrong names, and nothing it can use. The memory tears open like paper, exposing the machinery underneath.’
9. Give him his rule: ‘This place cannot remember you well enough to lie about you. Once in each scene, you may ask, What doesn't belong? I will reveal something real the realm is trying to hide.’
10. As they hit the tavern floor, use the shield's whisper: ‘The thief is trapped inside me. Now, so are you. Find what it took before it learns how to leave.’
11. End with: ‘Every chair in the Elfsong is empty. The song is playing backward.’ Move to Scene 3.

WHAT IS REALLY HAPPENING
The shield's emergency prison caught Vhalrix, nearby witnesses, and things metaphysically tethered to the demon. The Unwritten was physically on the road; he did not teleport into the party. The realm has no shield-stored memories of him, and his wife sabotaged the memories Vhalrix stole from her. Reveal that explanation in Scene 4, not here.

IF THE PLAYERS STALL
Have the road repeat more violently: the same crow flies past backward, the same blood lands twice, and Candlekeep shrinks. Then trigger the shield's scream and the fall.

DO NOT FORGET
• Record the wife's name and recognized object.
• Tell the Unwritten his once-per-scene question aloud.
• Do not use ‘Is that your answer?’ in this scene; no meaningful decision is being locked.

CUT FOR TIME
Limit falling memories to one sentence each. Preserve the Unwritten's arrival, his special rule, and the shield's whisper.

scenes.title: The Elfsong Played Backward
scenes.purpose: Let the players reconstruct the campaign chronology themselves and introduce the three-Truth structure.
scenes.readAloud:
The tavern is empty, but every chair is pulled out as though its occupant stood at the same instant. Four scorched pictures hang above the bar: a singing tavern, a bathhouse door, prisoners at a noble table, and a shield disappearing down the road.

The pictures twitch, rearrange themselves, and begin telling your story incorrectly.
scenes.secrets:
The correct order is Elfsong, bathhouse, Vanthampur capture and Brody's death, then the stolen shield on the Candlekeep road. Vhalrix deliberately depicts Brody abandoning the party, the bathhouse as a failure, and the party willingly giving away the shield. Every time the players correct a lie, the realm becomes less stable.

DAX — Through a window, Dax sees the night he watched Flaming Fist soldiers shove civilians against a wall, steal their coin, and strike anyone who objected. Only Dax initially recognizes it.
scenes.notes:
AT A GLANCE
Goal: let the players rebuild the campaign chronology themselves, reject four false versions of their history, give Dax a private choice, and award the first Truth.
Timebox: 20 minutes.
End condition: the four portraits are in order and corrected; the party has Truth of the Song; the Unwritten notices a fifth portrait.
This is a recap, not a test of the players' real memory. Supply facts freely when needed.

BEFORE YOU START
• Prepare a physical token or note labeled Truth of the Song: cancel one group fear, illusion, or psychic effect in the finale.
• Be ready to send Dax's private text without reading it to the table.
• Remember the correct order: Elfsong → bathhouse → Vanthampur capture and Brody's death → demon steals the shield on the Candlekeep road.

RUN IT STEP BY STEP
1. Read the Read aloud text. Point out that the four frames can be lifted and moved.
2. Let the players inspect them. The shield whispers: ‘It cannot change what happened. It can only convince you to remember differently.’
3. Ask them to arrange the frames chronologically. Do not deal damage for mistakes. A wrong arrangement simply shudders apart and becomes more obviously false.
4. Whenever they place a frame, ask one person: ‘What actually happened here?’ One central fact is enough.
5. When a correction is true, describe the painted lie burning away, the real memory appearing beneath it, one verse of the song becoming intelligible, and one chain breaking around the exit.
6. Try to hear from several players, but accept actions, short answers, or ‘My character points to this one’ as participation. Do not demand speeches.
7. After correcting the Elfsong frame, run Dax's private moment below.
8. When all four are corrected, award Truth of the Song and explain its exact mechanical use. Place the token where everyone can see it.
9. End by revealing the fifth backward portrait only to the Unwritten. Move to Scene 4.

PORTRAIT CHEAT SHEET
1 — ELFSONG: The false painting shows a cheerful drinking song while the party laughs. Truth: the song was a real warning even before they understood it.
2 — BATHHOUSE: The false painting shows the party fleeing while the cult remains victorious. Truth: they entered, cleared the threat, and left the optional undead army buried.
3 — VANTHAMPUR TABLE: The false painting shows Brody abandoning an otherwise sensible party. Truth: the party was captured; Amrik warned them their behavior would get someone killed; Brody and Ori mocked the danger; Brody died. Beneath the corrected table sits the mysterious shield, but the hands that placed it there have been burned out of the image. Preserve the mystery of why they were meant to carry it.
4 — STOLEN SHIELD: The false painting shows the party ceremonially giving the shield to Vhalrix. Truth: the demon took it after they failed to stop the theft; they did not willingly surrender it.

USING THE UNWRITTEN
If he asks, ‘What doesn't belong?’ identify the clearest counterfeit detail in one portrait. He cannot provide the party's history, but he can see where the constructed memory has seams. If the group is stuck, remind him of the question once.

DAX — PRIVATE MESSAGE
Send or hand him: ‘You recognize this night. You watched Flaming Fist soldiers torment these people while you studied their patrols. You told no one—not what they did and not how deeply you came to hate them. The memory has noticed you watching it.’

DAX — VHALRIX'S PRESSURE
Privately say: ‘You despise their cruelty, yet hide that hatred from your companions. Is it their violence you fear—or what you might do if given permission?’ This is a dishonest binary. Ask, ‘What does Dax do with the memory?’

DAX — VALID RESPONSES
He may reveal what he saw, enter the portrait and protect the civilians, steal a Fist insignia as evidence, admit his hatred, reject Vhalrix's framing, close the curtain, or deliberately keep the memory private. When his intent is clear, ask ‘Is that your answer?’ Any deliberate response reclaims ownership of the memory and earns Broken Fist: once in the finale, destroy one Memory Husk or break one restraint on an ally. Public confession is not the correct or required answer.

IF DAX ACCEPTS THE FRAME
If he confirms that he wants permission to hurt people, record Vhalrix's Claim — Permission. Use it later only as a taunt or the appearance of a Memory Husk; never force Dax to attack or remove the player's control. He still earns Broken Fist for giving a deliberate answer.

FAIL FORWARD
If nobody remembers an event, state the objective fact and ask, ‘What part of that does your character remember most clearly?’ If they try to destroy the portraits, the frames break open and expose the truthful images beneath; destruction becomes a valid method of correction. The door opens once the four truths are acknowledged in any form.

REWARD — TRUTH OF THE SONG
Say: ‘The warning was real, even before you understood it.’ Explain: surrender this token during the finale to cancel one group fear, illusion, or psychic effect.

TRANSITION TO SCENE 4
After the exit unlocks, tell the Unwritten: ‘There are five frames on the wall now. The fifth is hanging backward. You are certain it was not there before.’

CUT FOR TIME
State the correct order after one failed attempt. Ask for one correction per portrait, run Dax's choice, award the Truth, and reveal the fifth frame. Do not cut the Dax decision or Scene 4 transition.

scenes.title: The Fifth Portrait
scenes.purpose: Reveal the fate of the Unwritten's wife, explain why Vhalrix cannot rewrite him, and give him a concrete reason to descend into Avernus with the party.
scenes.readAloud:
The fifth frame is warm beneath your fingers. When you turn it over, you recognize the wallpaper before you recognize the room. Your bedroom waits inside the painting exactly as it did on the night she vanished—except that your side of the bed has been carefully erased.

Her body lies on the floor beside it. She is dressed for sleep. She has been dead far longer than this impossible room has existed. Above her heart is a coin-shaped burn, empty at its center.

From somewhere behind the walls, Vhalrix whispers, 'She worked so hard to make me forget you. And still, you came.'
scenes.secrets:
This is her real body, not an illusion or a test. Vhalrix abducted her to feed on her memories while preparing for the shield theft. She resisted by giving it contradictory versions of her husband until his identity became a blind spot in every memory Vhalrix carried. It killed her, sold her soul through an infernal market in Avernus to be minted into a soul coin, and kept her corpse tethered as a trophy. When the shield imprisoned Vhalrix, the body was pulled inside with it.

Her soul is not destroyed and is not inside this realm. Nothing available in the one-shot can resurrect her while her soul remains bound in Avernus. Her body will be expelled onto the Candlekeep road when Vhalrix dies, whether or not the party physically carries it through every scene. Recovering the soul coin is a future campaign objective and the Unwritten's reason to remain with the party.
scenes.notes:
AT A GLANCE
Goal: reveal exactly what happened to the Unwritten's wife, show that her resistance made him Unwritten, establish that her soul coin is somewhere in Avernus, and present one fair confirmed choice.
Timebox: 15 minutes.
End condition: he knows the body is real, the soul is absent but recoverable in Avernus, and his response to Vhalrix's offer has been recorded; then the bedroom dissolves into the bathhouse.
This is not a mystery puzzle. Give the essential facts without requiring successful rolls.

WHAT IS TRUE
• The corpse is his real wife's physical body.
• She died before the contained Hell formed.
• Vhalrix abducted and killed her while feeding on her memories.
• She protected her husband by giving Vhalrix contradictory versions of him. That is why this realm cannot write him correctly.
• Vhalrix sold her soul into Avernus, where it was minted into a soul coin. Her soul was not destroyed.
• Nothing in tonight's pocket realm can resurrect her because her soul is elsewhere. Recovering the coin becomes a future campaign goal.
• Her body will return to the road when Vhalrix dies, even if the party cannot carry it through every scene.

BEFORE YOU START
• Have the wife's name and recognized personal object in front of you.
• If you have not already done so before the session, make sure the player is comfortable with his missing-wife story ending tragically. Do not spring irreversible backstory harm on a player who did not consent to that tone.
• Prepare two possible rewards: Her Voice and Vhalrix's Tooth.
• Do not ask for a check to recognize her or determine whether she is dead.

RUN IT STEP BY STEP
1. Tell the Unwritten that only he notices the fifth frame hanging backward. Let him decide whether to turn it around or ask someone else to do so. The scene waits; do not punish hesitation.
2. When it turns, read the Read aloud text. Replace generic references with his wife's name whenever possible.
3. State plainly: ‘This is her real body. She is dead.’ Do not soften it into ‘appears dead’ and do not make him roll.
4. Stop speaking. Give the player several seconds to respond. Accept silence, touching the body, covering her, anger, investigation, or asking questions. Do not demand a monologue.
5. When the player is ready—or if the table begins filling the silence for him—say that the room is beginning to replay the final memory Vhalrix took from her.
6. Run Her Final Memory below. This answers why the realm cannot remember him.
7. Point out the coin-shaped burn above her heart. Resolve Evidence of Avernus below. The group must learn that her soul became a soul coin even if every check fails.
8. After that truth lands, Vhalrix makes its offer. Explain exactly what it can and cannot do before asking for confirmation.
9. Ask the Unwritten what he does. When his response is clear, ask, ‘Is that your answer?’
10. Resolve the matching branch, record the decision and reward in Quick capture, allow a brief farewell or action, then transition to the bathhouse.

HER FINAL MEMORY — READ OR PARAPHRASE
‘The bedroom resets around you. Black fingers press against her temples. Vhalrix commands, Show me the one who will come looking. She gives it the wrong face. It asks again; she gives it another. Again. Another. At last the demon screams, Who is he? She smiles through the blood in her teeth and says, Someone you'll never see coming.’ Then the memory ends and only the body remains.

EVIDENCE OF AVERNUS
The coin-shaped brand is ringed with Infernal script: ‘Assayed. Rendered. Remitted below.’ Anyone proficient in Arcana or Religion recognizes an infernal soul assay automatically. Otherwise allow DC 12 Arcana or Religion—but failure only means the shield must explain it. The shield reluctantly confirms: Vhalrix sold her soul into Avernus to be forged into a soul coin. It does not know the coin's current owner or location.

VHALRIX'S OFFER
Say: ‘Give me one true memory of her, and I will let what remains of her speak once.’ Then clarify out of character if needed: Vhalrix cannot resurrect her, contact her real soul, or bring the soul coin here. It can animate an extremely convincing imitation assembled from stolen memories. The player may ask questions before answering.

IF HE GIVES A TRUE MEMORY
Ask for one specific, ordinary memory rather than his most traumatic one. The imitation rises, speaks in her voice, and may answer one emotional question using only knowledge she possessed before the abduction. End the echo with: ‘Whatever wears my face after this is not me. Find the coin.’ Record Vhalrix's Claim — Beloved Detail: once in the finale, Vhalrix may invoke that detail to force him to reroll a successful saving throw. Give him Her Voice: once in the finale, after seeing a failed save against Vhalrix, he may turn it into a success. Both effects happen; sharing is neither purely rewarded nor purely punished.

IF HE REFUSES
The imitation never rises. Beneath his wife's hand is a black tooth she tore from Vhalrix during the abduction. Give him Vhalrix's Tooth: once in the finale, after Vhalrix declares a legendary action, he may cancel it completely. Refusal may be spoken or expressed through a clear action such as covering her face, turning away from the apparition, or attacking the memory.

IF HE FINDS ANOTHER ANSWER
Allow a strong physical, magical, or character-specific response. Reveal the Avernus information regardless and award a one-use benefit roughly equal to an automatic save or cancelled legendary action. Do not make sharing his grief the correct solution.

IF THE PARTY INTERFERES
Remind them gently: ‘This offer is waiting for his answer.’ Other characters may comfort, advise, or stand beside him, but they cannot make the decision. If they pressure him, ask them to give the player room.

DEPARTURE
Let him cover, hold, search, or speak to the body. Do not rush immediately after his answer, but call the scene at 15 minutes. Describe the bedroom wallpaper running like wet paint and becoming bathhouse tile. Everything turns to memory except the corpse. The shield says: ‘Kill the thief and what is real will leave with you.’

RECORD BEFORE MOVING ON
• Wife's name and recognized object.
• Gave memory / refused / another answer.
• Reward: Her Voice, Vhalrix's Tooth, or custom equivalent.
• Whether Vhalrix gained Beloved Detail.

CUT FOR TIME
Preserve four beats: reveal the real body, play her final resistance, establish the soul coin in Avernus, and resolve Vhalrix's offer. Cut extended investigation and shorten the farewell; never cut the Avernus revelation.

scenes.title: Bathhouse of the Unraised
scenes.purpose: Revisit a genuine party victory, provide a fast opening fight, and give Morn a personal contribution.
scenes.readAloud:
The tavern floor softens beneath your boots and becomes wet tile. The bathhouse has returned, but every pool is filled with ash. Around an infernal brazier stand the dead you left beneath Baldur's Gate—silent, armed, and waiting for an order you never gave.

A voice behind their teeth says, 'You left an army sleeping. Say the word now, and I will give you the strength you were too frightened to claim.'
scenes.secrets:
The offer is false: Vhalrix cannot give the party a lasting army, only make them responsible for these trapped echoes. Refusing the army causes the Ossuary Brute to form from the brazier. Accepting also starts combat, but Vhalrix calls the decision consent. Either way, extinguishing the braziers frees the dead.

MORN — His shield contains a vial labeled 'For those you could not bring home.' He did not place it there. Using it on a brazier automatically extinguishes that brazier and makes the dead soldiers salute before vanishing.
scenes.notes:
AT A GLANCE
Goal: turn a real past victory into a short combat puzzle, let Morn free people he could not save, and award Truth of the Dead.
Timebox: 20 minutes; aim for two or three rounds.
End condition: all three braziers are extinguished or the encounter is decisively won; the dead are released; the party has Truth of the Dead.

BEFORE YOU START
• Open the linked Bathhouse of the Unraised encounter and use Add party.
• Default opposition: Ossuary Brute plus two Unraised Dead. Use all four Dead if Jon attends or the group is cruising.
• Prepare a physical token or note labeled Truth of the Dead: when someone would fall unconscious in the finale, they remain at 1 HP instead.
• Remember Morn's shield contains a vial labeled ‘For those you could not bring home.’ He did not place it there.

RUN IT STEP BY STEP
1. Read the Read aloud text. Make the three infernal braziers visually obvious: one beside the brute and one at each end of the ash-filled pools.
2. Let the party answer Vhalrix's offer. If they treat accepting or refusing the army as a serious character choice, clarify that the voice promises power but has not shown it can keep that promise. Then ask, ‘Is that your answer?’ Record the answer, but combat begins either way.
3. Show the lie immediately. If they refuse, ash builds the Ossuary Brute. If they accept, the dead turn toward them awaiting impossible orders while the same brute forms; Vhalrix says, ‘Then their obedience is yours.’ Do not give Vhalrix control of a character.
4. Start initiative. Tell the players plainly: ‘The dead are tethered to those three braziers. You can fight them, extinguish the fires, or try something else.’
5. At the top of each round, state how many braziers remain and describe the dead suffering rather than behaving like eager soldiers. Keep the objective visible.
6. On Morn's first turn, tell him privately or aloud: ‘Something knocks inside your remedy shield. A vial you never packed is labeled: For those you could not bring home.’ Let him decide what it means and how to use it.
7. Run the Brute aggressively enough to create urgency, but aim its first attacks at sturdy characters. The Dead spread out to threaten concentration or block routes; they are not HP sponges.
8. When the first brazier goes dark, one group of dead lowers its weapons. When the second goes dark, the Brute cracks and loses confidence. When the third goes dark, all remaining Dead salute or bow and collapse; the Brute loses its second attack.
9. End combat once the outcome is certain. Do not spend table time grinding the Brute's last HP if all three braziers are out.
10. Award Truth of the Dead and explain its exact finale use. Then describe the wet tile lengthening into a polished Vanthampur dining table and move to Scene 6.

BRAZIER OPTIONS
A character may use an action and succeed with DC 14 Athletics, Arcana, or Religion. Holy water, a healing remedy, 10 radiant damage, Morn's mystery vial, or another strong physical or magical solution also works. The vial succeeds automatically. Reward good ideas instead of policing the list.

ENEMY CHEAT SHEET
Ossuary Brute — AC 14, HP 60, speed 30 ft. Multiattack: two Slams. Slam: +6 to hit, 2d8 + 4 bludgeoning. The first time it falls below 30 HP, two more Dead emerge unless at least two braziers are already out.
Unraised Dead — AC 12, HP 1, speed 30 ft. Rusted weapon: +4 to hit, 5 damage. Any damage destroys one; a sensible area attack may destroy several.

IF THEY IGNORE THE BRAZIERS
After round one, have a dead soldier rasp, ‘Not us. The fire.’ Point a skeletal hand toward a brazier. If they still choose pure damage, allow it. The Brute's threshold summons two more Dead and the encounter ends when the enemies are defeated. They still learn the factual Truth, but describe the echoes being destroyed rather than peacefully released.

MORN'S MOMENT
Using the vial is a contribution, not a confession. When it extinguishes a brazier, the dead soldiers recognize Morn, salute, and vanish without accusation. Vhalrix may whisper, ‘They forgive you so easily because they are not real.’ Morn may answer in words or actions. If it becomes a serious answer about accepting or rejecting responsibility, use the confirmation rule. Do not require him to absolve himself.

FAIL FORWARD
Failed checks flare painfully but reveal the correct method; let another character try. If the party is in real danger, the shield can hiss, ‘Break the anchors, not the memories,’ making the braziers unmistakable.

REWARD — TRUTH OF THE DEAD
Say: ‘You entered the bathhouse. You survived what waited below. You left the optional army buried instead of claiming it.’ Explain the token: surrender it in the finale when a character would fall unconscious; that character remains at 1 HP instead.

RECORD BEFORE MOVING ON
• Accepted or refused Vhalrix's army offer, if confirmed.
• Whether Morn used the mystery vial.
• Truth of the Dead awarded.

CUT FOR TIME
Start with only the Brute and two Dead. At the end of round two, let the next extinguished brazier snuff the others in a chain reaction. Preserve Morn's vial prompt, the factual Truth, and the reward.

scenes.title: The Warning They Ignored
scenes.purpose: Recap the Vanthampur capture and Brody's death without turning the adventure into a lecture.
scenes.readAloud:
You are seated at a Vanthampur table beneath chandeliers made from executioner's blades. Amrik sits opposite you, looking exhausted rather than surprised. Ori occupies one chair. Beside him is an empty place set for Brody.

Amrik raises a glass. 'Let me try this warning one more time.'
scenes.secrets:
The room is a repeating execution, not a conventional fight. If the party attacks Amrik, narrate the executioner's blade falling and reset them immediately at the table. Do this only once before revealing alternative routes. Amrik is an echo, not the real man, and Vhalrix wants the party to waste time fighting him.

Brody's empty chair is the important detail. On escape it falls backward, revealing his silhouette being dragged through a door of fire.
scenes.notes:
AT A GLANCE
Goal: replay the ignored warning without lecturing the players, let them escape a repeating execution by listening or acting intelligently, and award Truth of the Warning.
Timebox: 20 minutes.
End condition: the party escapes the loop; Brody's empty chair reveals where his memory went; the party has Truth of the Warning.
This is not a normal combat. Do not open initiative.

BEFORE YOU START
• Prepare a physical token or note labeled Truth of the Warning: turn one successful attack against a party member into a complete miss during the finale.
• Decide which escape option best matches each likely player so you can offer concrete clues.
• Limit the execution reset to one. Repetition should clarify the puzzle, not waste time.

RUN IT STEP BY STEP
1. Read the Read aloud text. Emphasize Ori's occupied chair and Brody's empty place without explaining them yet.
2. Have Amrik say calmly: ‘You have been captured by the Vanthampurs. Mock me if you need to, but understand this: continue treating this as a joke and one of you will be killed. There will not be another warning.’
3. Ask: ‘What does your character remember happening at this table?’ Supply the facts if memories are hazy: they were captured instead of investigating; Amrik warned them; Brody and Ori mocked him; Brody died. This is a recap, not a quiz.
4. Let the party respond. They do not need to apologize, agree with Amrik, or perform remorse. Listening, searching, stealing, breaking the mechanism, and rejecting the false script are all legitimate.
5. If someone attacks Amrik, the blade chandelier drops. Describe one sharp flash, then reset everyone into their original chairs with Amrik raising the same full glass. Do this once only. On the reset, make escape clues obvious.
6. Say: ‘The wine has refilled, the blade is clean, and Amrik is repeating the same breath. This room wants the warning to end in exactly the same death.’
7. Let any escape option below work. Ask for at most one roll per approach; a good resource or especially apt action may simply succeed.
8. As the exit opens, Brody's chair falls backward. Its shadow becomes Brody's silhouette being dragged through a door of fire. Say: ‘The realm did not invent his death. It has been saving the shape it left behind.’ Do not yet say he can return.
9. Award Truth of the Warning and explain its exact finale use.
10. Transition: beyond the fire-door is a colorless battlefield filled with upright shields. Move to Scene 7.

ESCAPE OPTIONS
• Listen until Amrik finishes without interrupting the warning; the ordinary door unlocks.
• Steal the executioner's keys: DC 14 Sleight of Hand.
• Identify and disrupt the repeating script: DC 14 Investigation, Insight, Arcana, or an apt psionic approach from Ori.
• Break the room's supports: DC 17 Athletics or 15 damage to each of two pillars.
• If Jon attends, the barred gate is physically real; DC 20 Athletics tears it from the wall. Another character can help. Let this be the impossible-strength spotlight he enjoys.
• If the Unwritten asks what does not belong, reveal that Amrik casts no reflection. Walking through the reflection exits the loop.
• Accept another plan that demonstrates they understand the room is a script rather than a fight.

IF THEY MOCK AMRIK AGAIN
Let the joke land, then have Amrik remain tired and direct. Do not treat table humor as a locked choice. If a player deliberately turns the warning into a serious character decision, clarify the immediate stakes and ask, ‘Is that your answer?’ Record the response for Vhalrix's later taunts, but never recreate Brody's death as an out-of-character punishment.

IF THEY KEEP FIGHTING
After the single reset, attacks pass through Amrik like smoke while the execution mechanism remains solid. Say: ‘You can destroy the room, but there is nothing alive here to kill.’ Point them toward the keys, pillars, gate, reflection, or simply hearing the warning out.

IF THEY STALL
Amrik says, ‘You keep preparing your answer before I finish the question.’ If needed, address the Unwritten: ‘Amrik appears in every silver surface except one.’ Then reveal the reflection exit without a roll.

DO NOT REQUIRE
An apology, confession, agreement that the players deserved what happened, or a solemn speech. The Truth is factual: capture, warning, mockery, death. The meaningful action is refusing to reenact Vhalrix's preferred ending.

REWARD — TRUTH OF THE WARNING
Say: ‘The Vanthampurs captured you. Amrik warned you. Brody died after he and Ori refused to take the danger seriously.’ Explain the token: surrender it in the finale after an attack succeeds against a party member; the attack becomes a complete miss.

RECORD BEFORE MOVING ON
• How the party escaped.
• Any serious confirmed response to Amrik's warning.
• Truth of the Warning awarded.

CUT FOR TIME
Skip the reset. After Amrik gives the warning, expose the keys, damaged pillars, barred gate, and missing reflection at once. Let one chosen approach succeed, reveal Brody's silhouette, and award the Truth.

scenes.title: The Ledger of the Dead
scenes.purpose: Give Morn and Dax optional emotional beats, reveal Brody, and let Brody's player experience both characters before choosing.
scenes.readAloud:
The dining room opens onto a battlefield beneath a colorless sky. Thousands of shields stand upright in the mud. Each bears the name of someone its owner failed to save.

Morn recognizes soldiers from another life. Dax finds one shield with no name—only the print of a Flaming Fist boot. Korrath finds one shield bearing two names.

BRODY ‘BRO’ BROHAN
KORRATH DRAKENSCALE
scenes.secrets:
The nameless shield represents the civilian Dax saw during reconnaissance; their ultimate fate remains unknown, leaving a future campaign thread rather than inventing a death. Morn's failed soldiers do not accuse him. Vhalrix wants him to accuse himself.

Brody does not know whether he is a soul, a preserved memory, or a possibility made real by the shield. He knows he is himself and wants to live. He will not demand Korrath's sacrifice.
scenes.notes:
AT A GLANCE
Goal: give Morn and Dax optional emotional beats, reveal Brody as a thinking person rather than a prize, and let Brody's player inhabit both characters before the finale.
Timebox: 20 minutes.
End condition: Brody is stabilized and joins the coming battle as an Echo; the player understands how Brody and Korrath share a turn; nobody has yet been told about the final trade.

BEFORE YOU START
• Confirm Brody's Echo is already listed in The Shield's Crucible encounter, but do not add him to the active fight yet.
• Have Brody's short combat rules available: speed 30 ft.; Greataxe +6, 1d12 + 4; Reckless Attack; Rage twice for +2 melee damage and physical resistance.
• Remember: Morn's soldiers do not blame him. Dax's nameless shield does not prove the civilian died.
• Give Brody and Korrath's player room to respond without telling them a choice is coming.

RUN IT STEP BY STEP
1. Read the Read aloud text slowly. Name Morn, Dax, and Korrath as each sees the shield meant for them.
2. Start with Morn. Describe familiar unit insignia, dents, or handwriting among the named shields. Ask, ‘What does Morn do when he sees them?’ Accept silence, touch, prayer, anger, medical ritual, or another action.
3. If Morn listens, the shields say variations of: ‘You did not command the battle,’ ‘You carried who you could,’ and ‘We are not asking you to join us.’ Vhalrix wants Morn to supply the accusation himself; the dead do not accuse him.
4. Move to Dax. His shield has no name, only a Flaming Fist boot print. Tell him privately if useful: ‘You cannot tell whether this marks a victim, a survivor, or simply the moment you chose to watch.’ Let him engage or leave it untouched. Do not force disclosure of his reconnaissance.
5. Move to Korrath's shield. The two engraved names separate like doors. Brody falls out between them, wounded, breathing, and confused. Give the player a moment to see the original character again.
6. Speak as Brody: ‘I don't know if I'm a soul, a memory, or something this place made because none of you knew what to do with my death. But I know I'm still me.’
7. To Korrath, have Brody add: ‘I want out. I'm not going to lie about that. But I don't need you to die just because I did.’ He means this. Do not make Brody manipulative.
8. Ask the table: ‘How do you stabilize him?’ Morn's remedy, a healing spell, a potion, a donated Hit Die, Medicine, or another caring action works. Do not let missing resources block Brody's return to the scene.
9. Once stabilized, give Brody's player two or three minutes to speak or act as Brody. Prompt with one question if needed: ‘Brody, what is the first thing you need to know?’ Then let the table respond.
10. Explain the finale mechanic only: ‘When Brody's chains break in the next scene, Brody and Korrath will share one turn. Each round, you choose which one acts.’ Do not reveal that only one can leave.
11. Transition: the field splits beneath the two-name shield, exposing the broken road and Vhalrix wrapped around the stolen shield. Move straight to Scene 8.

MORN — IF HE BLAMES HIMSELF
Let him speak, then answer through one soldier he remembers: ‘Carry us if you must. Do not pretend you killed us so the world will finally make sense.’ If Morn takes a serious position about whether his failure defines him, clarify the stakes and use ‘Is that your answer?’ Record it for a brief finale callback. Do not make self-forgiveness mandatory.

MORN — IF HE WILL NOT ENGAGE
A shield tilts just enough to uncover the mystery vial's empty slot. That confirms the dead helped him in the bathhouse. Then let him move on without penalty.

DAX — OPTIONAL BEAT
The nameless shield is an unresolved thread, not proof of a death. If Dax touches it, show the civilian escaping into an alley while Flaming Fist boots pass by; the memory ends before their fate is known. If Dax destroys or turns away from it, accept that answer. This scene must not expose his secret to the party unless his player chooses to do so.

STABILIZING BRODY
Any credible act of aid succeeds. If everyone freezes, the Unwritten can see that the wound is stitched with red memory-thread rather than blood; cutting the thread or speaking Brody's name stabilizes him. If they attack Brody, the weapon passes through while the injury worsens, proving that violence is not the interaction. Morn's shield then produces enough remedy to complete the stabilization.

BRODY ROLEPLAY PROMPTS
Use only one if conversation needs help:
• ‘Who made it out after I died?’
• ‘How long has it been for you?’
• To Korrath: ‘Did they give you my bedroll too?’
• ‘Where were we going before everything went wrong?’
Keep Brody angry, alive, and capable of humor. He is not omniscient and does not know the final rule.

BRODY'S ECHO CHEAT SHEET
Speed 30 ft. Greataxe: +6 to hit, 1d12 + 4 slashing. Reckless Attack. Rage twice: +2 melee damage plus resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing. Brody and Korrath share one turn; the player chooses one of them to act each round.

DO NOT REVEAL YET
Do not say ‘only one can leave,’ ask the player to choose, imply Korrath must die, or let the party debate the trade. Scene 9 explains the permanent decision privately after the battle.

RECORD BEFORE MOVING ON
• Morn's confirmed answer, if any.
• Whether Dax engaged with the nameless shield or disclosed anything.
• How Brody was stabilized.
• One thing Brody said or learned that the finale can echo.

CUT FOR TIME
Give Morn and Dax one concise image each, then move immediately to the two-name shield. Preserve Brody's opening, one response from his player, stabilization, and the shared-turn rule.

scenes.title: The Shield's Crucible
scenes.purpose: Pay off the recovered Truths in a mobile final battle, defeat Vhalrix, and reclaim the stolen shield.
scenes.readAloud:
The battlefield tears down its center. The road to Candlekeep rises from the wound in broken slabs, suspended over fire. At its far end hangs the stolen shield, bound in chains made from tavern song, bathhouse bone, and an executioner's warning.

Wrapped around it is a many-limbed demon chewing through metal that screams with every bite. Vhalrix looks up with your memories running like blood from its mouth.

'You have carried this prison long enough,' it says. 'Let me show you what it was teaching you to become.'
scenes.secrets:
Vhalrix is trying to consume the imprisoned intelligence, not release it. The shield will whisper useful tactical advice but always frame itself as the party's indispensable ally. Do not reveal its full identity unless that matches the campaign's established knowledge.

At half HP, Brody's chains break and his Echo joins initiative. If Dax earned the Broken Fist, one Memory Husk resembles a Flaming Fist enforcer. Dax may crush the token to destroy it or break a restraint on an ally. The personal object the Unwritten recognized on the road still hangs among Vhalrix's trophies and falls beside his wife's body when the demon dies.

UNWRITTEN PAYOFF
If he gave Vhalrix a true memory of his wife, he has Her Voice and may turn one failed saving throw against Vhalrix into a success. Vhalrix also has Beloved Detail and may once force him to reroll a successful saving throw. If he refused, he has Vhalrix's Tooth and may cancel one legendary action after it is declared.
scenes.notes:
AT A GLANCE
Goal: deliver a mobile final battle that pays off every reclaimed Truth, breaks Brody free at half HP, kills Vhalrix, and returns the stolen shield.
Timebox: 45 minutes. Call the fight by minute 40 so Scene 9 has room to breathe.
End condition: Vhalrix is dead; the shield, the wife's body, and her personal object are recovered; the realm begins collapsing into the final choice.

BEFORE YOU START
• Open the linked Shield's Crucible encounter and use Add party.
• Set Vhalrix's HP: 110 for four characters, 135 for five, 160 for six or more.
• Use one legendary action per round for four characters; two for five or more.
• Begin with two Memory Husks; add a third for six or more. Brody's Echo starts present in the tracker but chained and unable to act.
• Put Truth of the Song, Truth of the Dead, Truth of the Warning, Broken Fist, and the Unwritten's reward where you can see them. Cross off only the rewards actually earned.
• Note whether Vhalrix has Beloved Detail from Scene 4 and any answer it can taunt from Morn, Dax, or the bathhouse offer.

RUN IT STEP BY STEP
1. Read the Read aloud text. Point out three physical facts: Vhalrix is wrapped around the shield at the far end; memory-chains anchor the road; Brody hangs bound beneath the central slab.
2. State the objective plainly: ‘Kill Vhalrix to recover the shield. Breaking memory-chains can disrupt the battlefield. Brody is trapped but alive enough to react.’
3. Roll initiative. Vhalrix starts near the shield, Husks start between it and the party, and the party starts together on the first road slab. Avoid spending time on exact distances unless the group enjoys maps.
4. At the start of round one, remind the group that their Truth tokens are one-use answers to the realm. Read each token's effect once.
5. On Vhalrix's turns, keep it moving. Use claws against exposed or sturdy targets, then climb or Scuttle so melee characters must pursue. Use Stolen Memory when it can hit at least three characters.
6. At initiative 20, trigger the next memory hazard from the rotation below. Announce the source before resolving it so the matching Truth feels earned rather than guessed.
7. Have Husks block routes, threaten restrained characters, and resemble earlier lies. If Dax earned Broken Fist, one is unmistakably a Flaming Fist enforcer.
8. The first time Vhalrix reaches half HP, stop briefly. Brody's chains snap. Tell Brody/Korrath's player: ‘Starting now, they share your turn. Each round, choose whether Brody or Korrath acts.’ Add Brody to the active flow; do not reveal the final choice.
9. In the second half, use one personal callback per round at most. Vhalrix can mimic the wife's voice, invoke Morn's soldiers, or accuse Dax. Keep taunts short so the fight keeps moving.
10. If Vhalrix has Beloved Detail, use it once after the Unwritten succeeds on an important save: describe one perfectly remembered gesture and require the reroll. Immediately remind the player that Her Voice can later turn one failed save into a success.
11. When Vhalrix falls, stop initiative. Describe it vomiting the shield onto the road. The wife's body becomes fully real nearby and her personal object falls from Vhalrix's trophies beside her.
12. Say: ‘The road is collapsing, but the exit is open.’ Then read or paraphrase Scene 9's opening.

ROUND-BY-ROUND GUIDE
Round 1 — Establish movement and use the Elfsong hazard. Vhalrix claws or Scuttles; do not unload every ability immediately.
Round 2 — Use Stolen Memory if charged and the bathhouse-hands hazard. Let Vhalrix react to the first Truth spent.
Round 3 — Use the Vanthampur-chain hazard. Vhalrix should approach half HP; release Brody as soon as the threshold is crossed.
Round 4 — Make it personal. Use a character payoff, Husks, and aggressive claws.
Round 5+ — Stop adding complications. Focus all play on Vhalrix and drive toward the kill.

VHALRIX CHEAT SHEET
AC 16. HP by party size: 110 / 135 / 160. Speed 40 ft., climb 40 ft. Saves: Dex +6, Con +7, Wis +5. Resistant to fire, cold, lightning, and psychic. Advantage on saves against spells and magical effects.
Multiattack — two Rending Claws.
Rending Claw — +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., 2d6 + 4 slashing plus 1d6 psychic.
Stolen Memory, Recharge 5–6 — 30-foot cone, DC 14 Wisdom; 4d8 psychic on failure, half on success; failed creature loses reactions until its next turn.
Legendary: Scuttle — move half speed without opportunity attacks.
Legendary: Claw — make one Rending Claw.
Legendary: Rewrite Failure, costs 2 — one creature makes DC 14 Wisdom save or has disadvantage on its next attack or save.

MEMORY HUSK CHEAT SHEET
AC 13, HP 10, speed 30 ft. Attack: +4 to hit, 1d8 + 2 slashing. Their appearances echo old enemies, victims, or a Flaming Fist enforcer. They protect Vhalrix and create movement pressure; do not play them as tactical geniuses.

INITIATIVE 20 — ROTATE IN ORDER
1. Deafening Elfsong — DC 14 Wisdom or frightened until next round. Announce, ‘The warning-song becomes a command.’ Truth of the Song cancels it for everyone.
2. Bathhouse hands — DC 14 Strength or Dexterity or restrained until the creature uses an action to escape. Describe hands rising from ash-filled pools.
3. Vanthampur chains — +6 to hit, 2d8 force and pull 10 feet. Announce the executioner's chain before rolling. Truth of the Warning turns a successful hit into a miss.
Repeat only if needed. Truth of the Dead triggers whenever someone would fall unconscious.

PLAYER PAYOFFS
• Truth of the Song: cancel the group Elfsong fear/psychic effect.
• Truth of the Dead: leave one falling character at 1 HP.
• Truth of the Warning: turn one successful attack against a party member into a miss.
• Dax — Broken Fist: destroy one Memory Husk or break one restraint on an ally.
• Unwritten — Her Voice: turn one failed save against Vhalrix into a success. If Vhalrix has Beloved Detail, it may force one successful save reroll first.
• Unwritten — Vhalrix's Tooth: cancel one legendary action after it is declared.
• Morn: the soldiers' shields may intercept one visual effect when he acts in accordance with his recorded answer; keep this narrative unless the party needs help.

IF THE PARTY IS OVERWHELMED
Have the shield give useful but self-serving advice: ‘The song answers the song. Use what you reclaimed.’ Let a broken chain deal 10 damage to a Husk or free a restrained character. Reduce Vhalrix's remaining HP by up to 20 without announcing the adjustment, or stop using damaging legendary actions. The goal is pressure, not a wipe before the permanent decision.

IF THE PARTY IS STEAMROLLING
Add one Husk, use vertical movement, and spend every allowed legendary action. Do not inflate HP beyond the selected band. Their preparation and tokens should matter.

CUT FOR TIME
At minute 35 of this scene, remove remaining Husks and stop initiative 20 hazards. At minute 40, the next solid hit kills Vhalrix or breaks the last chain so the shield tears it apart. Preserve Brody's half-HP entrance, at least one Truth payoff, and the recovery of the shield, body, and object.

RECORD BEFORE MOVING ON
• Which Truths and personal rewards were spent.
• One memorable action from Brody and one from Korrath.
• Confirm shield, wife's body, and personal object recovered.

scenes.title: One Story Leaves
scenes.purpose: Give Brody and Korrath's player a clear, private, consequential choice, return the campaign to the Candlekeep road, and leave the Unwritten with a concrete trail toward his wife's soul in Avernus.
scenes.readAloud:
The shield strikes the broken road with a sound like a prison door closing. Beyond it, daylight opens onto the road to Candlekeep. One by one, your companions become solid beneath that distant sky.

Brody and Korrath do not. Between them stretches a single shadow. The realm has made space for one continuing story, and the doorway will not carry both.
scenes.secrets:
The party cannot solve this with a spell, check, bargain, sacrifice from another character, or vote. Brody's restored existence occupies the same thread of continuation as Korrath. When the contained Hell collapses, only one name can be carried through. The rejected continuation is consumed completely: no body, soul, afterlife, prison, or echo remains. Resurrection, divine intervention, Wish, contact with the dead, and a later rescue cannot restore that character. The party still remembers the person who ceased.

Korrath is the living character and therefore has metaphysical priority. If the player refuses to choose, cannot choose, or does not actively surrender Korrath, Korrath returns and Brody ceases forever. Returning as Brody requires the player to knowingly and voluntarily end Korrath.

The opportunity is the surprise. The permanence is not. Explain the exact finality of both outcomes privately before asking the player to choose. Once confirmed, do not reverse it.
scenes.notes:
AT A GLANCE
Goal: give Brody and Korrath's player a private, informed, permanent choice; honor the result without loopholes; and return the survivors to the Candlekeep road with the next campaign threads clear.
Timebox: 15 minutes. Protect at least 10 minutes for this scene.
End condition: the player has chosen or defaulted to Korrath; exactly one character crosses; the party wakes with the shield and the wife's body; Candlekeep and the soul coin in Avernus are explicit next steps.

BEFORE YOU START
• Take Brody/Korrath's player aside, message them privately, or give them two written options. Do not conduct the decision by public vote.
• Have both character sheets available. If Brody returns, he returns at level 5.
• Be ready to explain the metaphysics in plain language. The surprise is the opportunity, not hidden consequences.
• Remember the default: unless the player knowingly and voluntarily ends Korrath, Korrath survives and Brody ceases.

RUN IT STEP BY STEP
1. Read the Read aloud text to everyone. Then tell the table: ‘The next part belongs privately to their player. Give us a moment; nobody else can make or solve this choice.’
2. Speak privately: ‘The realm can carry one continuing story through the exit: Korrath or Brody. Because Korrath is currently alive, he returns by default.’
3. State the finality exactly: ‘This is not imprisonment. The one who does not cross is consumed when the realm ends. There will be no body or soul to resurrect, contact, Wish back, bargain for, or rescue later. Everyone will still remember them.’
4. State the options: ‘Keep Korrath, and Brody's second chance ends forever. Explicitly surrender Korrath, and Brody returns fully alive at level 5 while Korrath ends forever. If you refuse or cannot choose, Korrath returns.’
5. Invite factual questions. Answer anything about what the character understands, the immediate stakes, character level, or permanence. Do not argue for either result.
6. Ask: ‘Which story crosses?’ When the player answers, repeat it plainly, then ask, ‘Is that your answer?’ Only the confirmed answer is final.
7. If Brody is chosen, require an explicit confirmation that the player understands Korrath will not remain available in any form. If the answer is ambiguous, the default remains Korrath.
8. Ask the player for one final image, action, or line from the character who ends. A short answer or ‘he just nods’ is enough. Never demand a speech.
9. Return to the table and narrate the selected branch below. Do not disclose private deliberation unless the player wants to.
10. Ask each player once: ‘What does your character remember that nobody else does?’ Go around the table without cross-talk; each may answer briefly or pass.
11. Narrate the road epilogue: the survivors wake outside the collapsed realm with the stolen shield recovered, the wife's real body beside the Unwritten, and her recognized personal object resting on her chest or in his hand. Candlekeep finally draws closer.
12. Restate both next objectives: Candlekeep may reveal what the shield is and why Hell wants it; the coin-shaped burn and Vhalrix's records point toward the wife's soul coin somewhere in Avernus. End on the shield's whisper: ‘Now that we remember one another, perhaps you are finally ready to learn what I am.’

KORRATH LIVES
Brody looks at Korrath and says, ‘Then make it worth being the one who got up.’ He may offer a forearm clasp, crooked grin, insult, or silent nod chosen by the player. Brody then becomes red sparks drawn into the collapsing road. He leaves no soul, ghost, echo, or recoverable fragment. Korrath crosses fully alive and remains the player's character. Optional boon: once per long rest, Korrath gains advantage on one Strength check or melee attack in memory of the decision.

BRODY LIVES
The player must explicitly confirm that Korrath voluntarily surrenders his continuation and will never be available again. Ask for Korrath's final action or words. His outline passes through Brody like armor closing around a body, then disappears completely. No soul or echo remains. Brody crosses fully alive at level 5. Retire Korrath's sheet permanently after the session; do not leave him deactivated as a recoverable option.

NO CHOICE OR AMBIGUOUS CHOICE
Korrath crosses automatically. Brody says, ‘I wanted another chance. I didn't want it to become another thing this place made you carry.’ He then ceases with the realm. Do not ask repeatedly until the player sacrifices Korrath. The default protects the living character.

IF THE PARTY TRIES TO INTERVENE
Say: ‘You can see them, but your voices cannot cross the single shadow. This is not a vote.’ Do not accept another soul, a spell slot, a check, a bargain with the shield, or another character's sacrifice. Let the party react after the choice, but stop anyone from pressuring the player.

IF THE PLAYER ASKS FOR A LOOPHOLE
Answer directly: there is none inside the fiction or waiting in the campaign. Divination confirms the rule but does not change it. Wish, resurrection, divine intervention, infernal bargains, cloned bodies, memories, and later quests cannot restore the consumed continuation. If the player does not accept that cost, Korrath lives.

TONE CHECK
Give the player enough quiet to decide, but do not perform grief at them. Brody wants to live and Korrath is not disposable; neither answer is morally correct. The finality should feel heavy because it is understood, not because information was withheld.

THE UNWRITTEN'S EPILOGUE
His wife's body is real and can be carried or preserved. Her personal object is returned. The empty coin-shaped burn and any infernal mark or record recovered from Vhalrix establish that her soul was minted into a soul coin in Avernus. She cannot be resurrected while the coin binds her, but the trail is actionable. This is why the Unwritten can remain with the party when they continue toward Avernus.

RECORD AFTER THE SCENE
• Final character: Brody or Korrath.
• If Brody returned, set him to level 5 and permanently retire Korrath.
• If Korrath remained, permanently close Brody's return thread.
• Wife's name, body recovered, object recovered, soul coin lead established.
• Each character's final private memory, if useful for future sessions.

CUT FOR TIME
Never cut the private explanation, factual questions, or ‘Is that your answer?’ confirmation. Cut the round-robin memory question and shorten the road description if necessary. Preserve the permanent result and the Candlekeep/Avernus next objectives.

encounters.title: Bathhouse of the Unraised
encounters.notes:
DEFAULT FIELD
Ossuary Brute plus two Unraised Dead. Use all four Dead if Jon attends. Run for two or three rounds; ending the hazard matters more than grinding every HP.

THREE BRAZIERS
A character extinguishes one with an action: DC 14 Athletics, Arcana, or Religion; holy water; a healing remedy; 10 radiant damage; or another strong physical solution. Morn's mystery vial automatically extinguishes one. When all three are out, every remaining Unraised Dead collapses and the Brute loses its second attack.

OSSUARY BRUTE
Speed 30 ft. Multiattack: two Slams. Slam: +6 to hit, 2d8 + 4 bludgeoning. The first time it falls below 30 HP, two additional Unraised Dead emerge unless at least two braziers are already extinguished.

UNRAISED DEAD
Speed 30 ft. Rusted weapon: +4 to hit, 5 damage. Any damage destroys one. A sensible area attack may destroy several.

OUTCOME
Extinguishing the braziers frees the echoes and awards the Truth of the Dead. The token leaves one falling character at 1 HP in the finale.

encounters.title: The Shield's Crucible
encounters.notes:
SCALING
Vhalrix has 110 HP for four characters, 135 HP for five, or 160 HP for six or more. Use one legendary action per round for four characters and two for five or more. Begin with two Memory Husks; add a third for six or more characters. Add the live party before starting.

VHALRIX THE RECALL-EATER
Speed 40 ft., climb 40 ft. Saves: Dex +6, Con +7, Wis +5. Resistant to fire, cold, lightning, and psychic damage. Advantage on saves against spells and magical effects.
Multiattack: two Rending Claws.
Rending Claw: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., 2d6 + 4 slashing plus 1d6 psychic.
Stolen Memory (Recharge 5–6): 30-foot cone, DC 14 Wisdom save, 4d8 psychic on a failure or half on a success. A creature that fails cannot take reactions until its next turn.
Legendary — Scuttle: move half speed without opportunity attacks.
Legendary — Claw: make one Rending Claw.
Legendary — Rewrite Failure (costs 2): one creature makes a DC 14 Wisdom save or has disadvantage on its next attack or save.

MEMORY HUSKS
Speed 30 ft. Attack: +4 to hit, 1d8 + 2 slashing. Let their appearances echo old enemies, victims, or a Flaming Fist enforcer.

INITIATIVE 20 — ROTATE THESE HAZARDS
1. Deafening Elfsong: DC 14 Wisdom or frightened until next round. Truth of the Song cancels it for everyone.
2. Bathhouse hands: DC 14 Strength or Dexterity or restrained until the creature uses an action to escape.
3. Vanthampur chains: +6 to hit, 2d8 force and pull 10 feet. Truth of the Warning negates the hit.
Truth of the Dead triggers when someone would fall.

BRODY'S ECHO
At half Vhalrix's HP, Brody's chains break. Brody and Korrath share one turn; their player chooses who acts each round. Brody: speed 30 ft.; Greataxe +6 to hit, 1d12 + 4 slashing; Reckless Attack; Rage twice for +2 melee damage and physical resistance.

VICTORY
Vhalrix vomits up the shield and the contained Hell collapses into the final Brody/Korrath choice.
